transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-12-08
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Redwood: Samir Patel (AE), Clara Liu (SE)
Customer: Jasmine Ortiz (Procurement), Leo Nakamura (Security), Anika Bose (Legal), Raj Verma (CTO)
Recording id: ff-20271208-8472

Summary: Quick workshop to align on MSA/DPA exceptions, SLO targets (billing impact), and onboarding path for a pilot. Focus on dedicated vs hosted, KMS options, SOC2 artifacts, and procurement timing.

Topics: onboarding path, SLA vs SLO language, pricing buckets, dedicated capacity sizing, KMS/HSM options, audit logs and retention, PO timing

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samir (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you clearing time. Happy holidays in advance. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Jasmine (Procurement): Jasmine here.
[00:07] Leo (Security): Leo here.
[00:09] Anika (Legal): Anika on the line.
[00:10] Raj (CTO): Raj, CTO.
[00:11] Samir: Great. Clara, quick intro?
[00:14] Clara (SE): Hi all, Clara Liu, I'm the solutions engineer focused on performance and private deployments; I'll go through the dedicated sizing later.
[00:20] Samir: Agenda — align on MSA/DPA redlines Anika's flagged, discuss SLO targets and how they map to pricing, KMS and data residency, then next steps.

[00:40] Raj: Quick context — Cobalt's intent is to run customer-facing LLM features for financial advisors. We have strict retention and audit requirements, and must decide between Redwood hosted API with VPC egress or Dedicated capacity in our VPC. Key constraint is we need per-request auditability and separation of envs.

[01:05] Leo: Security: SOC2 is table-stakes, but we also need evidence of key rotation policies, KMS integration, and support for customer-managed keys (HSM) for certain PII flows. Also curious about KV cache persistence and whether customer tokens ever hit Redwood logs.

[01:28] Clara: Short answers — we support customer-managed KMS via our Private offering; for Redwood Dedicated you can bring your VPC and we can configure KMS/HSM integration. KV cache terminology — apologies, sometimes speech to text flips it to KV cash — it's ephemeral by default and kept in-memory unless configured for warm start; we don't persist raw prompt text in logs unless retention is enabled.

[01:50] Anika: On the MSA redlines, we've flagged three clauses: data processing/transfer, indemnity cap, and escrow clause. Also the SLA section uses 'best efforts' in fallback descriptions which we want tightened to clear SLOs and remedies.

[02:12] Samir: Totally reasonable. For SLOs we typically provide tiers — e.g., Platinum: 50ms median token latency, 99.9% availability for inference endpoints; Gold: 75ms median, 99.5% availability; Silver: higher latency, 99% availability. Pricing differs substantially as you bump up reserved capacity and priority routing.

[02:45] Jasmine: Procurement needs clearer language tying SLAs to credits and the invoice adjustments process. The MSA currently says 'service credits may be issued' — can we get a more prescriptive formula?

[03:03] Samir: Yes, we can add schedule with credit calculation per downtime minute and cap per month. I'll surface our standard SLA credit schedule. Clara, do we have that doc?
[03:12] Clara: I do — I'll send the SLA schedule. Note that for Dedicated we also offer an uptime SLA tied to node replacement. For Private on-prem there's different fallback terms.

[03:30] Leo: About logs and audit — does Redwood provide token-level tracing in the Console? We need immutable audit logs for requests for three years for certain regulated products.

[03:45] Clara: We provide request-level traces and per-route logs; retention is configurable and we can integrate with your log archive (S3/GCS). There's a cost for long-term retention; we typically ship exports to customer bucket with object-level immutability if requested.

[04:05] Anika: KMS — we require Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) for production and want to ensure that in the DPA the key control paragraph shows customer sole possession of keys.

[04:18] Samir: We can add explicit language in the DPA about BYOK for Private/Dedicated with key wrapping and zero-knowledge handling. I'll coordinate with product/infosec to get the exact wording.

[04:40] Raj: On the infra side, we need a sense of the burst policy. Most of our traffic is spiky in market open hours; how do you handle bursts beyond reserved capacity? Do we get throttled or auto-burst to shared pool?

[05:00] Clara: We offer burst capacity: Dedicated customers can configure burst to hosting pool tier with pre-negotiated limits. There's also auto-fallback to a lower-cost model variant which changes latency and output quality subtly — we can configure fallback policies and alerts. Also prefix caching helps with repeated prompts.

[05:25] Raj: What's the delta in cost if we want 99.9% availability vs 99.5%?

[05:33] Samir: Roughly a 20-35% premium depending on instance type and reservation term because you pay for guaranteed headroom and priority routing. Clara will run a tailored estimate.

[06:00] Jasmine: Procurement question — do you require an initial commit or can we start with a month-to-month pilot? Also need clarity on PO windows and invoice terms (net30 vs net45).

[06:18] Samir: We can do a month-to-month pilot on Hosted with usage billing; Dedicated typically requires a quarterly reserved commitment for pricing to be attractive. PO terms are flexible: we support net30 standard, can do net45 with enterprise contract.

[06:40] Anika: On indemnity, our counsel asks for a mutual cap linked to fees. Is Redwood open to that?

[06:50] Samir: That's negotiable for enterprise deals; we typically propose a cap equal to 12 months' fees for unlimited time customers, but for regulated customers we can discuss higher caps under enterprise support tiers. I'll note that as negotiable.

[07:10] Leo: Encryption in transit + at rest — confirm TLS 1.2+; also FIPS endpoints for KMS?

[07:20] Clara: TLS 1.3 in our hosted endpoints; KMS endpoints can be FIPS-compliant in our Private offering when integrated with your HSM.

[07:35] Raj: For the PoC we will want to run a load test that simulates peak trading volumes; can Redwood run a benchmark against the prospective model with our traffic profile?

[07:48] Clara: Yes — if you provide sample traffic patterns (p50/p90 token lengths, qps distribution), we can run a benchmark on our Dedicated staging cluster and share token-level cost/latency breakdown. That usually takes 5 business days.

[08:10] Jasmine: Action for procurement — we need a final pricing worksheet that shows hosted vs dedicated cost for 3 forecast profiles and the SLA tiers. Can you add estimated monthly credit exposure if SLOs are missed?

[08:28] Samir: We'll include that. Clara will produce the worksheet and a cost sensitivity analysis.

[08:45] Anika: On DPA and data residency — we have EU customer data that must remain in EU regions and be processed under EU DPA terms. What options exist?

[08:58] Samir: We can provision region-specific Dedicated clusters and ensure no egress. Our Private control plane can be hosted in your EU region or on-prem. DPA exhibits can enumerate region scoping.

[09:15] Leo: Any third-party subprocessors? We need a subprocessor list and notification timing for changes.

[09:22] Samir: Yes we maintain a subprocessors registry and notify customers on changes typically 30 days in advance for material changes. We'll include the current registry in the security pack.

[09:45] Raj: About metrics — we need tail latency numbers (p95/p99) not just median. Does Redwood publish tail latency for model catalog items?

[09:55] Clara: We publish model profiles that include median and tail percentiles per sequence length bucket. For Dedicated the tail varies by node sizing; we'll provide a p99 estimate for your profile in the benchmark.

[10:20] Jasmine: Billing nuance — if we push logs to our S3 archive for three years, is that additional storage on top of your fees or included?

[10:30] Samir: Long-term archival is billed as an add-on: storage + export fee. We'll show a line item in the worksheet for archival cost.

[10:50] Anika: Can you confirm redaction options? Some PII must be redacted before logs leave Cobalt's environment.

[10:58] Clara: Yes, you can apply pre-request redaction or use our local preprocess step in Private deployment to strip PII before hitting the inference path. We'll document options.

[11:25] [small cross-talk]
[11:40] Samir: Ok, quick dive into the MSA language — Anika, can you highlight the specific paragraph numbers you want tightened?
[11:48] Anika: Section 6.2 (SLA credits), 9.1 (Indemnity), and 12.4 (Data transfer). We'll email redline.

[12:05] Samir: Good. We'll produce a redline-friendly exhibit with proposed alternative wording.

[12:18] Raj: For the PoC we want a 45-day evaluation, targeted at a single region with dedicated nodes but no long-term commitment; will Redwood accept that?

[12:30] Samir: We usually support 30–60 day pilot arrangements; for Dedicated pilot we can do a 45-day reserved trial at reduced rate if you commit to a follow-on negotiation window.

[12:48] Jasmine: Procurement also asks: who signs the MSA? We need to know Redwood's contracting authority for >$1M and whether electronic signature is acceptable.

[12:58] Samir: Electronic signature accepted; for deals >$1M we have VP-level signatory. I'll include contact info for contracting in the packet.

[13:20] Leo: One more security question — do you do quarterly pen tests and share reports under NDA?

[13:28] Samir: Yes, we do internal and third-party penetration tests annually; summary reports are available under NDA and SOC2 reports are shareable. Specific pen-test reports are by request under NDA.

[13:45] [pause]
[14:00] Clara: I'm going to summarize the technical deliverables we'll provide: 1) Dedicated sizing recommendation with burst config, 2) Benchmark run with your sample traffic, 3) Tail latency/cost spreadsheet, 4) Export procedures for audit logs, 5) KMS integration checklist.

[14:20] Raj: Great. For bench we will provide token length and qps histograms and a synthetic load harness; prefer to do the bench on the 4th of next week.

[14:30] Jasmine: Procurement timeline — we want final commercial terms before EoY if possible. Internal budget cadence is next week so we'll try to accelerate.

[14:40] Samir: Noted. We will prioritize the packet.

[14:55] Anika: On DPA exceptions — one ask: data subject access requests routing; we need Redwood to flow requests to our team within 48 hours.

[15:05] Samir: We can add 48-hour routing for DSARs in the exhibit. I'll flag with privacy team.

[15:20] Leo: Also need role-based access (RBAC) scoping for production vs staging; ensure least privilege.

[15:28] Clara: RBAC is in Console with token-level roles; for Dedicated we can map to your IdP via SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning.

[15:45] Jasmine: Any open items we missed?

[15:50] Samir: Let's recap. Actions: Samir send security pack + DPA suggested language; Clara send sizing and cost worksheet + SLA schedule; Raj send traffic profile; Anika send MSA redlines; Jasmine confirm procurement timeline and PO terms. We'll schedule PoC kickoff week of Dec 20 if the packet looks good.

[16:15] Jasmine: That works. Thanks all.
[16:20] Raj: Thanks.
[16:22] Anika: Thanks.
[16:24] Samir: Thanks everyone, I'll follow up with minutes and attachments.
